builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Sparse Recovery Bird's-Eye View Model Soup for Robust Camera-Based 3D Object Detection
summary: The method replaces standard dense fine-tuning of camera-based BEV detectors (e.g., Fast-BEV) with a soup of sparse-recovered models: layer-wise magnitude-based random pruning creates diverse sparse variants, each is retrained with a randomly sampled learning rate, and their weights are averaged into a single dense model with no architectural or data changes. The cost is additional training compute for multiple recovery runs (a hyperparameter count per soup), though inference cost is unchanged and no extra data or hardware is required. Failure modes include reliance on mode connectivity that may not hold for other architectures, pruning rates, or datasets, and robustness gains validated only on nuScenes corruptions may not transfer to other sensor suites, tasks, or deployment domains.
rationale: The technique is computationally feasible on a single 24 GB GPU since it involves retraining moderate-size BEV detectors rather than foundation models, but the robustness gains are validated on one benchmark and one baseline, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: Sparse Recovery Model Soup for Robust BEV Detection

The cost is additional training compute for multiple recovery runs (a hyperparameter count per soup), though inference cost is unchanged and no extra data or hardware is required. Up to 33.8% improvement in corruption robustness and 1.8% gain in clean accuracy over the Fast-BEV baseline on nuScenes, with zero inference overhead.
